P1.reason: A covers every statement with recognizable rules (win/end, board, moves, turns, roles); B leaves most ungrouped and mixes x/o terminal and goal arbitrarily.

differences.reason: Helps: one coherent rule for lines, game end and winning, though large.
Helps: board setup and cell persistence form a clear board-state rule.
Helps: marking a blank cell and its effect is the core move rule.
Helps: alternating turns with x first is a clean, named rule.
Helps: players listed as their own small rule.
Neutral: diagonal lines as a sub-rule; slightly redundant inside A1.
Hurts: mixes row lines, x's terminal and o's goal; not one rule.
Hurts: ties diagonals to x's goal only, an arbitrary pairing.
Hurts: columns tied to o's terminal only; arbitrary split of the win rule.
Helps: full-board draw ending is a recognizable rule.
